guide.heading:
Guide to
Plot + Construction loan

cardData.title: Loan Sanction & Approval
cardData.para: The lender evaluates your income, credit score, and property documents to approve the loan amount, covering both the land purchase and construction costs.

cardData.title: Plot Purchase Disbursement
cardData.para: Once approved, the loan amount for buying the plot is disbursed first. The land must meet legal and location criteria set by the lender.

cardData.title: Construction Fund Release
cardData.para: The construction loan is disbursed in stages based on project progress, such as foundation, walls, roofing, and final completion, ensuring proper fund utilization.

cardData.title: Repayment & EMI Structure
cardData.para: Initially, you may pay interest-only EMIs during construction. Once completed, full EMIs (principal + interest) start, just like a regular home loan.

keyAdvantages.heading:
Plot & Construction Loan:
Key Advantages

list.heading: Lower Interest Rates –
list.desc: Compared to taking separate loans for land and construction, a combined loan usually offers a lower interest rate, making it more affordable.

list.heading: Easier Loan Management –
list.desc: Since it's a single loan, you don’t have to manage multiple EMIs, paperwork, or lenders. It simplifies the repayment process.

list.heading: Stepwise Fund Disbursement –
list.desc: The loan is disbursed in phases—first for the plot purchase, then for construction in stages. This ensures efficient fund usage and reduces interest burden initially.

list.heading: Tax Benefits –
list.desc: You can claim tax deductions on both principal repayment (Section 80C) and interest paid (Section 24B) after the construction is completed.

list.heading: Higher Loan Amount Eligibility –
list.desc: Lenders may offer a higher loan amount compared to standalone land loans, as the construction aspect makes it a secured asset.

list.heading: Longer Repayment Tenure –
list.desc: Unlike standalone land loans (which often have shorter tenure), this loan offers repayment terms similar to home loans, going up to 30 years, making EMIs more manageable.

list.heading: Better Approval Chances –
list.desc: Lenders prefer plot + construction loans over plot-only loans, as they ensure the land is utilized for home construction, reducing risks for the bank.

list.heading: Eligibility Criteria
desc: Age: 21 to 65 years (varies by lender).
Employment Type: Salaried, self-employed, or business owners.
Income Stability: Regular income with proof of salary slips or ITRs.
Credit Score: Minimum 700+ for easy approval.
Land Criteria: The plot must be non-agricultural and approved by local authorities.

list.heading: Affordability Criteria
desc: Loan-to-Value (LTV) Ratio: Up to 80-85% of the plot + construction cost.
EMI-to-Income Ratio: Ideally 50-60% of monthly income.
Down Payment: Minimum 15-20% of the total cost.
Interest Rates: Typically between 8% - 12% (varies by lender and credit profile).

list.heading: Credibility Criteria
desc: Creditworthiness: Good financial history with no loan defaults.
Employment Stability: Salaried individuals should have at least 2 years of job experience(below this contact us), self-employed applicants need 3+ years of business continuity.
Property Verification: The lender ensures legal clearance and approval from local development authorities.

contents.heading: Disbursement steps of Plot + Construction Loan

list.heading: 1. Construction Loan Approval
desc: Approved building plan from local authorities must submit
Construction cost estimate verified by an engineer/architect must submit
Builder agreement or self-construction plan must submit
Most lenders require construction to start within 1-2 years of plot purchase.

list.heading: 2. Plot Purchase Disbursement
desc: The first installment covers the cost of the land purchase.
The lender transfers this amount directly to the seller or landowner after verifying legal approvals.
The borrower may need to make a down payment (typically 15-20%).

list.heading: 3. Stage-Wise Construction Fund Release​
desc: Foundation & Plinth Work – First payout after site preparation
Walls & Structure Completion – Second payout after walls are raised
Roofing & Flooring – Third payout when structural work is nearing completion
Final Completion – Last payout after finishing work is done
Each stage is verified by the lender through site inspections.

list.heading: 4. EMI & Repayment Process
desc: Pre-EMI (Interest-Only Payments) – Until construction is completed, the borrower may only need to pay interest on the amount disbursed.
Full EMI Starts – Once construction is complete, full principal + interest payments begin, just like a regular home loan.

contents.heading: Balance Transfer for Plot + Construction Loan

list.heading: Eligibility for Balance Transfer–
list.desc:
Good repayment history on the current loan.
Credit score 750+ for better rates.
Construction progress proof required.
Stable income proof (salaried/self-employed).
Legally clear property with no disputes.

list.heading: Benefits of Balance Transfer–
list.desc:
Lower Interest Rates
Extended Loan Tenure
Top-Up Loan Option
Flexible Repayment Plans

list.heading: Steps to Transfer a Construction Loan–
list.desc:
Compare Lenders – Check interest rates, fees, and repayment terms.
Apply for Balance Transfer – Submit required documents (loan statement, income proof, property papers).
Loan Approval & Processing – The new lender will assess eligibility and approve the transfer.
Foreclosure of Existing Loan – Your current lender will close the loan, and the new lender will take over.
New Loan Agreement – You start repayment with the new lender under better terms.

topUp.heading: Top-Up Loan in Plot+Construction
topUp.para: A top-up loan in a Plot + Construction Loan is strictly meant for construction-related expenses and cannot be used to buy more land. Lenders provide this additional funding only to cover extra construction costs, interior work, or unforeseen building expenses.
